CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  November 15, 2021 -4:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  The meeting was convened and held virtually by videoconference/teleconference.

OPENING:  Vice Mayor Wilson called the meeting to order at 4 :31 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Julie Gutierrez, Assistant City
  Manager.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo (Absent)

  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda

  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

PUBLIC COMMENT  Steve Mermell, City Manager, reported that the agenda item related
  to housing overlay of church property is expected to return to the
  City Council after the first of the year: and with regard to the various
  investigations regarding the officer involved shooting of Anthony
  McClain, there is no update on the status at this time.

  The following individuals advocated for the City Council to address
  homelessness by providing affordable housing in the City; and
  spoke in support of the rezoning of land owned by churches to be
  permissible as "by-right" developments to increase the number of
  affordable housing units in the City:

  Sue Park-Hur, Pasadena resident
  Alli Burnison, Pasadena resident
  Rosalie Niemann, Pasadena resident

  The following individuals spoke on incidents involving Pasadena
  Police Officers, expressed concerns with the Pasadena Police
  Department, and the Department's policing policies; advocated for
  the termination of Pasadena Police Chief Perez, Officers
  Dumaguindin, Serrano, and Mulrooney, and/or City Manager Steve
  Mermell, and expressed concerns related to comments made by
  Mayor Gordo regarding public comment speakers:

  Hiram J. Cormier, Jr., Los Angeles resident
  Allen Shay, Pasadena resident
  Jason R., Los Angeles resident
  Kat Ross, representing Showing Up for Racial Justice (SURJ)

Council Minutes  11/15/2021
   Pastor Kerwin Manning, Pasadena resident
  Michael Williams, Pasadena resident
  Jane Ward, representing SURJ
  Akili (baba), representing Black Lives Matters Los Angeles

  Council member Hampton spoke on the need for the City Council to
  ensure that all residents of Pasadena feel safe in the City; and
  stated that he will continue to speak out when he deems it to be a
  matter of injustice and an issue of accountability, as he feels is the
  case with the officer involved shooting of Anthony McClain.

CONSENT CALENDAR  AUTHORIZE MODIFICATION OF THE RECOMMENDATION
  FOR THE PURCHASE ORDER WITH HAAKER EQUIPMENT
  FOR AN ADDITIONAL AMOUNT OF $221,147 TO UPGRADE
  ONE SEWER TRUCK MODEL PURCHASE
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that this action is exempt under the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) in accordance with Section
  15061(b)(3), the General Rule that CEQA only applies to projects
  that may have an effect on the environment; and
  (2) Authorize modification of the recommendation for the
  purchase order contract with Haaker Equipment Company
  (Haaker) for an additional amount of $221,147 to upgrade one
  sewer truck model purchase, increasing the total not-to-exceed
  amount from $700,269 to $921,416. Neither Competitive Bidding
  nor Competitive Selection are required pursuant to City Charter
  Section 1002(H) and Pasadena Municipal Code Section
  4.08.049(A)(3), contracts with other governmental entities.

  CONTRACT AWARD TO ELECNOR BELCO ELECTRIC, INC.,
  FOR PEDESTRIAN CROSSING ENHANCEMENTS PROGRAM
  FOR AN AMOUNT NOT-TO-EXCEED $175,000
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find the project proposed in the agenda report to be
  categorically exempt under the California Environmental Quality
  Act (CEQA) Guidelines in accordance with Title 14, Chapter 3,
  Article 19, Section 15301, Class 1, and Section 15303, Class 3.
  Class 1 consists of minor alterations of existing facilities, involving
  negligible or no expansion of use. Class 3 consists of construction
  of limited numbers of new, small facilities or structures. There
  would be no expansion of use of the street network as a result of
  the project, and therefore, there are no unusual circumstances; and
  (2) Accept the bid dated October 20, 2021, submitted by Elecnor
  Belco Electric, Inc., in response to the project plans and
  specifications for Pedestrian Crossing Enhancements on Marengo
  Avenue at Bellevue Drive and Raymond Avenue at Bellevue Drive
  project, reject all other bids received, and authorize the City
  Manager to enter into a contract for an amount not-to-exceed
  $175,000, which includes the base contract amount of $152,569

PUBLIC HEARING  PUBLIC HEARING: LINCOLN AVENUE SPECIFIC PLAN (LASP)
  UPDATE
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Adopt the Addendum to the 2015 Pasadena General Plan
  Environmental Impact Report (EIR) along with the EIR, and find that
  the Addendum properly discloses only minor technical changes or
  additions to the EIR, and none of the conditions triggering a
  subsequent or supplemental EIR are present, as set forth in State
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15164;
  (2) Make the Findings for Approval for the General Plan Map and Text
  Amendments, Specific Plan Amendment, and Zoning Code Map and
  Text Amendments;
  (3) Adopt a resolution approving the General Plan Map and Text
  Amendments;
  (4) Adopt a resolution approving the recommended Lincoln
  Avenue Specific Plan (LASP); and
  (5) Direct the City Attorney to prepare an ordinance for the Zoning
  Code and Text Amendments within 90 days consistent with the
  provisions set forth in the agenda report. (Resolution Nos. 9875,
  9876)
  PLANNING COMMISSION RECOMMENDATION: On June 23,
  2021 , the Planning Commission recommended that the City
  Council approve the proposed LASP, including the General Plan
  Map and Text Amendments, Zoning Code Map and Text
  Amendments, and the Addendum, as presented by staff, with the
  following recommended changes:

Council Minutes  5  11 /15/2021
   1. Amend the General Plan Land Use Diagram to allow housing in
  the LASP-CG zone within the Lincoln North Subarea;
  2. Prioritize streetscape enhancements within the Lincoln North
  Subarea, that improve pedestrian and bicycle safety and
  connections;
  3. Revise existing and/or add a new implementation program to
  explore the creation of a Business Improvement District to help fund a
  parking management program that reduces or eliminates parking
  requirements for individual properties and identifies other parking
  supply opportunities in the LASP-CG zone within the Lincoln North
  Subarea;
  4. Clarify the public open space requirements and consider
  renaming and/or including a definition in the LASP;
  5. Revise requirements specific to the Kettle's Nursery site located
  at the intersection of Wyoming Street and Lincoln Avenue and convert
  them into guidelines to support the redevelopment of the site and
  encourage preservation of the existing one-story midcentury structure
  on the northwest portion of the site; and
  6. Incorporate a goal and/or policy stating a preference to retain
  existing architectural style in the LASP-CG zone within the Lincoln
  North Subarea.

  City Manager Mermell and David Reyes, Director of Planning and
  Community Development, provided introductory comments, and
  Anita Cerna, Senior Planner, presented a PowerPoint presentation
  on the item, with all responding to questions.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, opened the public hearing; reported that
  the public hearing notice was published in the Pasadena Press and
  the Pasadena Journal on October 28, 2021, November 4, 2021 ,
  and November 11 , 2021; and that one letter in opposition to the
  staff recommendation was received by the City Clerk's Office,
  which was distributed to the City Council, posted on-line, and made
  part of the public record.

  Mr. Reyes reported that there is a correction to the staff report, and
  clarified that staff is not recommending to change the General Plan
  designation of any parcels, but rather to align the maximum densities
  of the amended specific plan parcels with the General Plan densities.

  The following individuals provided comments/suggestions on the
  matter:

  Pamela Wilson, member of Lincoln Avenue Christian Church
  Andrew Salimian, representing Pasadena Heritage
  Jill Shook, representing Making Housing and Community
  Happen

PUBLIC HEARING  PUBLIC HEARING: SUBMITTAL OF REDISTRICTING TASK
  FORCE  FINAL  REPORT  AND  RECOMMENDED
  REDISTRICTING PLAN FOR CITY COUNCIL CONSIDERATION;
  RECEIVE PUBLIC INPUT AND TESTIMONY ON THE
  REDISTRICTING PLAN AND THE COMPOSITION OF ONE OR
  MORE COUNCIL  DISTRICTS;  AND CONCEPTUALLY
  APPROVE OR MODIFY THE RECOMMENDED REDISTRICTING
  PLAN

Council Minutes  7  11/15/2021
   Recommendation of Redistricting Task Force:  It is
  recommended that the City Council, as part of a public hearing
  process in compliance with California Elections Code Section
  21627.1 , take the following actions:
  (1) Find that the proposed action is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to State CEQA
  Guidelines, Section 15061(b)(3), the Common Sense Exemption
  that CEQA only applies to projects that have the potential to have
  a significant effect on the environment;
  (2) Receive and review the Redistricting Task Force's
  recommended redistricting plan ("Redistricting Plan"), map, and
  related demographic data sheet (Attachment A - "Recommended
  Redistricting Plan approved October 30, 2021 by the Redistricting
  Task Force");
  (3) Receive public comment on the Redistricting Plan, and any
  public input/testimony regarding the composition of one or more
  council districts;
  (4) Conceptually approve the Redistricting Plan as submitted; or
  provide direction on requested modifications to the plan for further
  consideration; and
  (5) Continue the public hearing to each subsequent meeting of
  the City Council until December 6, 2021 , or such other date as the
  City Council may determine, at which time the City Council will be
  asked to close the public hearing and conduct first reading of "An
  Ordinance of the City of Pasadena Amending Chapter 1.20
  ("Election Districts") of the Pasadena Municipal Code" codifying the
  Recommended Plan as submitted, or a modified Redistricting Plan
  as directed by the City Council.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, opened the public hearing; reported that
  the public hearing notice was published in the Pasadena Press on
  November 1, 2021and the Chinese L.A. Daily News, La Opinion,
  Pasadena Press, and the Pasadena Journal on November 4, 2021.
  He also reported that the City Clerk's Office received (as of the last
  Redistricting Task Force meeting on October 30, 2021) one letter
  in support of minimal change map with 10% deviation, one letter
  expressing concerns and advocating for specific Council Districts
  for the Central District, one letter providing general comments and
  18 "Community of Interest" maps that were submitted by one
  individual, which were distributed to the City Council, posted on-
  line, and made part of the public hearing record.

  City Clerk Jomsky and Vince Farhat, Chair of the Redistricting Task
  Force (RTF), presented a PowerPoint presentation on the item, and
  responded to questions. Mr. Farhat thanked City staff, redistricting
  consultants, City Clerk Jomsky, RTF members and the community
  for all their hard work, support and input related to the RTF
  meetings and process. Mr. Jomsky thanked Chair Farhat, Vice
  Chair Moreno, and the RTF members for all their work on the City's
  RTF process.

Council Minutes  8  11/ 15/2021
   City Clerk Jomsky reported that there may be an error in the
  agenda report that will be corrected to reflect the correct shifts from
  District 6 to District 7 which includes: Del Mar Boulevard on the
  North, Los Robles Avenue on the West, California Boulevard on the
  South, and Madison Avenue on the East.

  David Ely, representing National Demographics Corporation
  (Redistricting consultants), provided information on census block
  boundaries (in the area adjacent to the 210 Freeway), noted that
  these lines are accurate in terms of the census blocks, do not
  contain any populations, and that will be cleaned up when the final
  map is created and distributed to the public; and responded to
  questions.

  The City Council thanked the Redistricting Task Force, the
  redistricting consultants, and City staff for the hard work and diligent
  efforts spent on the process.

  Councilmembers Masuda and Madison spoke in support of the
  Minimal Change with 10% Deviation Plan map.

  Councilmember Williams expressed concerns with the shift from
  District 7 to District 2, specifically with Oak Avenue and Roosevelt
  Avenue that are stop signs, unlike Craig Avenue that runs through
  without a stop sign that she believes connects communities. She
  stated that she does not believe a community is able to connect if
  you cannot cross the street.

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke on what he believes was a the
  thorough RTF process including community input, and spoke in
  favor of the Task Force recommendation of the Minimal Change
  with 10% Deviation Plan map and Redistricting Plan.

  Vice Mayor Wilson spoke in support of the redistricting line
  adjustment on Los Robles Boulevard and the Minimal Change with
  10% Deviation Plan map.

  Councilmember Rivas expressed concerns with the results of the
  2020 census and the undercount of Pasadena residents in the
  northwest part of the City.

  Motion:  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Madison,
  seconded by Councilmember Hampton, to continue the public
  hearing to November 22, 2021 at 5:00 p.m.:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton, Kennedy, Madison,
  Masuda, Rivas, Williams, Vice Mayor Wilson,
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Mayor Gordo
  ABSTAIN: None
